subject: Clarifying billing records access during DSRs — tax & audit considerations
messages:
From: Katie Barnes <katie.barnes@acme.com>

Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data subject deletion requests & billing records — quick clarification

Hi Mina,

Quick question from procurement before we move forward with signature: if an end user or contact in our account requests deletion under their local privacy law, what happens to invoices and usage exports that we rely on for tax/audit? Specifically:

- Will Acme still be able to access historic invoices tied to our account after a customer deletion request?
- Are usage logs / per-user token-level records deleted or redacted? We need to provide auditors with evidence of billable usage in some cases.
- Do you offer a way to export invoices and a certified attestation to present to our compliance team?

I'm attaching a short list of procurement questions for context. Appreciate a short written reply we can share with legal/tax.

Attachment: Acme_DSR_ask.pdf (PDF, 142KB)

Thanks,
Katie Barnes
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Katie Barnes <katie.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data subject deletion requests & billing records — quick clarification

Hi Katie — thanks for the clear questions and the attachment. Short answer up front: invoices and accounting-grade billing records required for tax and audit purposes are preserved under our accounting retention policy, even when individual end-user personal data is removed as part of a DSR.

A few details so your tax/audit team knows what to expect:

- Scope: We separate the financial ledger (invoices, payment receipts, billing ledger) from product-level user content. The ledger contains account-level identifiers, billing line items, taxes, and settlement metadata.
- What we remove: When a DSR requires erasure of personal data, we remove or redact PII tied to an individual (names, email addresses) in product logs and user records where feasible.
- What we retain for finance: Invoice PDFs, invoice numbers, billing account IDs, amounts, tax information, and a minimal set of non-sensitive metadata necessary to meet statutory obligations (we do not keep user plaintext content).
- Exports: We can provide invoice PDFs and CSV usage exports. Usage exports can be configured to include aggregated or granular rows; PII is redacted by default but we can provide token-level counts in aggregated form for auditors. See attached sample export.
- Attestation & timing: We can produce a short attestation letter about our policy and a certified invoice export within 3 business days upon request.

Next steps: if this meets your procurement needs, I can loop in Marissa (finance) to confirm retention windows and Vivek to confirm any exceptions for legal hold. Happy to schedule a 30-minute call early next week to finalize language for your vendor bind.

Attachment: invoice_export_sample.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data subject deletion requests & billing records — quick clarification

Hi Katie / team — passing along the finance-side detail Mina promised. I'm Marissa on Redwood Finance. A few practical notes and the policy baseline you can quote back to auditors: 

- Retention window: For statutory/tax compliance we retain accounting records for seven (7) years by default in the US. For EU customers we follow local statutory retention windows and will provide the applicable retention term.
- Ledger immutability: We do not delete invoice records that are part of the accounting ledger; instead, we redact PII fields as required and keep an immutable audit trail (invoice id, timestamps, amounts, tax lines).
- Usage vs billing: Token-level product logs (used for debugging and per-user tracing) are subject to deletion under DSRs. Billing exports used for invoicing and revenue recognition are preserved; when an invoice references a user identifier that must be erased, we replace that identifier with a non-reversible hash and retain the billing line.
- Legal hold / audits: If you anticipate audits or litigation, request a legal hold through your Redwood customer portal or via your CSM. Legal hold lifts the timeline for erasure for specified records while the hold is active.

If you need specific language for procurement, I can draft a 1-page statement saying: 'Redwood retains accounting-grade invoice records necessary for tax and audit purposes and redacts personal data in accordance with applicable law; exports and attestations are available upon request.' Tell me where to send the finalized wording and we'll prep it.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

2) We'd like a letter (brief) confirming Redwood's practice that invoice PDFs and accounting ledger entries will be available for Acme's audits even if individual user data is erased. Can you attach a draft we can review?

Katie — quick answers and next actions: 

- Granularity: We can provide exports at different granularities. By default we provide daily-aggregated rows for usage exports. Session-level exports (session start/end, token counts per session) are available as an opt-in export for customers with a legitimate audit need; those exports redact user-identifiable fields unless you request hashed identifiers under an agreement. Token-level raw logs (debug traces) are not preserved for DSR purposes.
- Draft attestation: Marissa will attach a one-page attestation draft to this thread. Expect language confirming invoice preservation and the redaction approach.
- Action plan: 1) Marissa to send draft attestation; 2) We’ll prepare a sample session-level export with hashed IDs for you to review (T+3 business days); 3) Schedule 30-min call — I'm available Tue/Wed AM PT.
